# 尊婆須蜜菩薩所集論

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Zūn Póxūmì Púsà Suǒjí Lùn* 尊婆須蜜菩薩所集論 (CBETA T28n1549) is a Former Qin (符秦) dynasty translation of a Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma text attributed to the Bodhisattva Vasumitra 婆須蜜 ([尊婆須蜜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%8A%E5%A9%86%E9%A0%88%E8%9C%9C)), 10 juan. It was translated by Saṃghabhūti 僧伽跋澄 ([僧伽跋澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E8%B7%8B%E6%BE%84)) and colleagues at Cháng'ān, with Zhú Fóniàn ([竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5)) serving as oral interpreter (*yì chuán* 譯傳). The colophon identifies it as 符秦罽賓三藏僧伽跋澄等譯. The preface to the text names Vasumitra (*Póxūmì* 婆須蜜, "friend of the Vasus") as a bodhisattva in the Maitreya lineage, predicted to become a future Buddha named "Lion Tathāgata."

**Abstract**

The text presents systematic Abhidharma instruction in the form of extended sets of definitions and classifications, organized into twelve thematic books (*jiāndù* 揵度). Its content overlaps substantially with the six-feet tradition, but the text is distinguished by its attribution to a Vasumitra identified as a *bodhisattva* — the term used in the preface suggests this Vasumitra is not the Kaśmīra council Vasumitra ([世友](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E5%8F%8B)) but a distinct figure with a devotional coloring. Modern scholarship (Willemen, Dessein, Cox 1998) treats this Vasumitra (*Upaśrī* Vasumitra, a.k.a. 尊婆須蜜 = *Zun-Póxūmì*) as a separate figure from the Vasumitra associated with the six feet.
